what: which defence ends a PHP corpus case on CheriBSD, measured instead of inferred
binary: controls/abort-probe.c, built purecap by the same flags as the port

platform.compiler: the CheriBSD SDK clang that built ports/php/cheribsd
platform.qemu: cheri-qemu from the SDK, run by run-cheribsd-cases.py

result.double free: SIGABRT (exit 134), NOTHING written to stderr -- byte for byte the signature of the 15 plain-temporal cases that read NO-READING:inconclusive
result.read after free: COMPLETES, and reads the old byte back

reading: Two things, both measured. (1) The aborts in the corpus are CheriBSD's own ALLOCATOR consistency check, not a capability fault: ktrace shows thr_kill(SIGABRT) with code=SI_LWP, the process raising the signal on itself, and this probe reproduces it from a plain double free. (2) At the platform default a use after free does not trap at all -- the chunk sits in quarantine, the stale capability is still valid and still reads the old bytes, because revocation is DEFERRED until a sweep. A short-lived CLI process can exit before any sweep runs. That is why the eager configuration (every free sweeps) turns 12 of those 15 into SIGPROT.
consequence: An abort may not be scored as CAUGHT on this arm: the arm measures CHERI, and what fired is a software check any allocator could carry. The judge keeps them as NO-READING and the bundle's notes name the defence.
